newsitem.title: UK: Oil plummets as gasoline slips into reverse.
newsitem.headline: Oil plummets as gasoline slips into reverse.

text.p: World oil prices tumbled on Tuesday, virtually wiping out two weeks of gains as U.S. gasoline markets slipped into reverse.

World benchmark Brent crude oil futures for July delivery ended 78 cents to trade at $19.22 a barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), led by a slide of over three percent in U.S. gasoline prices.
"(U.S.) unleaded gasoline was supporting the market last week," said a broker. "Now that's gone, everybody has an excuse to sell."

Brent crude rallied $1 a barrel during the past two weeks as U.S. refineries ratcheted up gasoline production in preparation for the unofficial start of the peak summer driving season, traditionally marked by Monday's Memorial Day holiday.
Investment funds also took advantage of bullish signals on price charts to build up substantial long positions in crude and product futures.
But with industry data suggesting flat demand and strong refinery production, the institutional investors were becoming increasingly isolated on the long side of the market, dealers said.
"There's a growing feeling that they may be long and wrong," said a broker in London.

While U.S. gasoline stocks remain nearly seven million barrels below levels seen this time last year, demand in 1997 is expected to rise a mere 0.3 percent promising a surprise windfall for the 82 percent of Americans who vacation by car.
"This year we don't get the call from members. They're not as worried about prices," said the American Automobile Association (AAA) spokesman Mike Morrisey last week.
Subdued demand growth in the U.S., by far the world's biggest importer of gasoline, has depressed oil refinery profits worldwide as product prices failed to maintain their premium to crude values.
Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell on Monday became the latest refiner to feel the pinch, trimming by about 15 percent crude throughput at its massive 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) Rotterdam plant.
Shell's move was in line with similar cutbacks recently at Esso Singapore's 230,000 bpd plant and at the huge 400,000 bpd British Petroleum/Texaco Nerefco complex, also in Rotterdam.
Refining margins in Asia shed some 65 cents a barrel last week, turning narrow profits at less simple plants into losses of about 37 cents a barrel.
